newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BNZ says better NZ data improves equities outlook.
newsitem.headline: BNZ says better NZ data improves equities outlook.

text.p: The investment managment unit of Bank of New Zealand (BNZ) said on Monday it had revised upwards its forecast of the estimated 12-month total return from New Zealand equities to 9.0 percent in the aftermath of benign inflation data last week.
"Economic growth is likely to bottom at 2.5 percent this quarter and New Zealand shares are increasingly attractive," the fund management group said in a statement.
"Our nine percent total return forecast includes a six percent dividend yield, but we believe capital growth risks lie on the upside," BNZ's head of investment management added.
"The new inflation numbers are very encouraging and lower the probability of the Reserve Bank needing to tighten monetary conditions later this year," Anthony Thyne added.
"This is positive for the local equity market in that it will help ensure a recovery in the economy next year," he said.
Thyne added the bank expected increased government spending would boost domestic fixed investment.

In the early part of this year a number of analysts made gloomy predictions for the New Zealand stock market in 1997, saying a volatile inflation outlook and the prospect of high interest rates would likely keep shares under pressure.
After last Tuesday's March quarter inflation data talk has turned to hopes for easier monetary conditions this year as money market rates have dropped across the yield curve.
